headline: Dhaka shaken by crude bomb blasts and bus arson
summary: Multiple explosions rocked Dhaka University and the CID headquarters, while three buses were torched in various parts of the city and outskirts.
details: Criminals exploded crude bombs in several areas of Dhaka, including inside Dhaka University and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) headquarters, and torched three buses in Bhatara, Dhamrai, and Savar.
A series of explosions rocked at least six different parts of Dhaka University, including the TSC area, Senate Building, and Nilkhet, occurring within minutes of each other around 6:42pm.
In Malibagh, a crude bomb was hurled into the CID headquarters compound from the Moghbazar-Mouchak Flyover, exploding near a Special Branch vehicle.
Another blast occurred in the Mirpur-1 area near Sony Cinema Hall, while a school bus in Bhatara and two other buses in Dhamrai and Savar were set ablaze.
Police detained three suspects—Rezaul Karim, Sohel Rana, and Nazmus Saad—after students caught them in the TSC area of Dhaka University.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) suspect a particular group is deliberately carrying out sabotage to create public panic, and several members of banned organizations have already been arrested.
Law enforcement has strengthened intelligence-led operations, increased police deployment, and introduced mobile patrols to ensure public safety.
Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage to identify individuals collecting flammable materials for the attacks.
caption:
Crude bombs and burning buses. Dhaka is under attack to create panic.

Criminals exploded crude bombs in several areas of Dhaka, including inside Dhaka University and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) headquarters, and torched three buses in Bhatara, Dhamrai, and Savar.

A series of explosions rocked at least six different parts of Dhaka University, including the TSC area, Senate Building, and Nilkhet, occurring within minutes of each other around 6:42pm.

In Malibagh, a crude bomb was hurled into the CID headquarters compound from the Moghbazar-Mouchak Flyover, exploding near a Special Branch vehicle.

Another blast occurred in the Mirpur-1 area near Sony Cinema Hall, while a school bus in Bhatara and two other buses in Dhamrai and Savar were set ablaze.

Police detained three suspects—Rezaul Karim, Sohel Rana, and Nazmus Saad—after students caught them in the TSC area of Dhaka University.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) suspect a particular group is deliberately carrying out sabotage to create public panic, and several members of banned organizations have already been arrested.

Law enforcement has strengthened intelligence-led operations, increased police deployment, and introduced mobile patrols to ensure public safety.

Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage to identify individuals collecting flammable materials for the attacks.

headline_marked: Workers seek [[over 30,000 taka minimum wage]] at board meeting
headline: Workers seek over 30,000 taka minimum wage at board meeting
summary: Garment workers' representatives will present their initial wage proposal today in the second meeting of the Minimum Wage Board.
details: The second meeting of the Minimum Wage Board is scheduled for today in Dhaka, where representatives of the ready-made garment (RMG) workers will submit their initial wage proposal.
Worker representative Babul Akhtar stated that after consulting with 12 coalitions, 60 federations, and various trade union leaders, they will propose a minimum wage exceeding 30,000 taka.
The Minimum Wage Board was formed by the government on November 1 following widespread worker protests demanding higher wages.
While some factories in Savar and Ashulia have seen a return to work, around 38 factories remained closed on Sunday due to ongoing unrest.
In Gazipur, tensions escalated as workers from Muntex Fabrics of the Mondol Group protested after their lunch break, leading to clashes with law enforcement.
Police and BGB members used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse workers who threw bricks and stones at security forces in Gazipur.
BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan noted that while protests have কমে এসেছে (have decreased), factory owners are eager to resume operations in factories that are not yet open.
caption:
Minimum wage proposal of over 30,000 taka! Garment workers are pushing for a major pay hike as the Minimum Wage Board meets today.

The second meeting of the Minimum Wage Board is scheduled for today in Dhaka, where representatives of the ready-made garment (RMG) workers will submit their initial wage proposal.

Worker representative Babul Akhtar stated that after consulting with 12 coalitions, 60 federations, and various trade union leaders, they will propose a minimum wage exceeding 30,000 taka.

The Minimum Wage Board was formed by the government on November 1 following widespread worker protests demanding higher wages.

While some factories in Savar and Ashulia have seen a return to work, around 38 factories remained closed on Sunday due to ongoing unrest.

In Gazipur, tensions escalated as workers from Muntex Fabrics of the Mondol Group protested after their lunch break, leading to clashes with law enforcement.

Police and BGB members used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse workers who threw bricks and stones at security forces in Gazipur.

BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan noted that while protests have কমে এসেছে (have decreased), factory owners are eager to resume operations in factories that are not yet open.
